title: The Version 2 exams, and what changed from Version 1
blurb: Know the V2 exam formats, how PRINCE2 Agile blends governance with agile delivery, and which V1 ideas to stop revising.
question: A colleague lends you a revision guide that says the PRINCE2 Agile Foundation exam has 50 questions, a 55% pass mark and five 'focus areas'. Can you trust it for the Version 2 exam?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile (Version 2) was launched in May 2025 with a new Official Book and new syllabi. It is examined at two levels. Foundation tests whether you can recall and understand the method. Practitioner tests whether you can apply and analyse it in a project scenario. Version 1, based on the 2015 guide, is being retired: the last day to sit a V1 exam is 31 December 2026, so every new candidate prepares for Version 2.
teach.cite: PeopleCert PRINCE2 Agile Foundation and Practitioner syllabi v2.0 (May 2025)

teach.h: Foundation and Practitioner side by side

rows.label: Prerequisite
values: Agile Foundation V2 or any V1 Agile

teach.caption: Practitioner adds one project scenario with an 'Additional information (People)' section. Neither exam uses negative marking.

teach.h: Where the 40 Foundation marks come from
teach.caption: Weightings 30%, 40%, 25% and 5%. Learning outcome 2 is the biggest slice.

teach.body: The book describes three areas of a project: project direction, project management and product delivery. Traditional project management is strong on governance and control but says little about product delivery. Agile is strong on product delivery and responding to change but light on direction and management. PRINCE2 Agile covers all three areas, keeping governance and control throughout, by tailoring PRINCE2 with agile mindset, frameworks, artifacts and workshops.

teach.caption: Some organizations still use PRINCE2 Project Management for governance alone, without agile delivery; the book recognizes that choice (3.1).

teach.h: Revise it, or leave it in the old guide?
teach.note: V2 spells the practice 'organization' and uses 'self-management' rather than 'self-organization'.

teach.h: Worked example: checking a borrowed guide
teach.body: At Kestrel Rail Services, analyst Priya Nair is booking her Agile Foundation exam. A colleague lends her a guide promising 50 questions, a 55% pass mark and chapters on 'focus areas' and the 'hexagon'. Priya checks the V2 syllabus: 40 questions, 24 to pass, 60 minutes, closed book. She sets the guide aside and revises the seven practices, seven aspects, 11 roles, artifacts and workshops instead.

teach.text: 50 questions with 28 to pass (55%) is the retired V1 Foundation format. V2 Foundation is 40 questions with 24 to pass (60%). Practitioner is 50 questions with 30 to pass in both versions, so do not mix the two.

items: Foundation V2: 40 questions, 24 to pass, 60 minutes, closed book, recall and understanding.
Practitioner V2: 50 questions, 30 to pass, 150 minutes, Official Book with your notes.
PRINCE2 Agile covers direction, management and delivery, with governance throughout.
V2 uses practices (not themes), seven aspects, 11 roles, agile artifacts and named workshops.

summary: You can now state the Version 2 Foundation and Practitioner formats and explain how PRINCE2 Agile blends project management with agile across direction, management and delivery. You can also spot Version 1 ideas that no longer belong in your revision.

A.q: What is the format of the PRINCE2 Agile Foundation (Version 2) exam?
A.why: Version 2 Foundation has 40 one-mark questions and the pass mark is 24 (60%).

whyNot.1: 50 questions with 28 to pass (55%) was the Version 1 Foundation format.
whyNot.2: 50 questions with 30 to pass is the Practitioner format.
whyNot.3: There are 40 questions, but the pass mark is 24, not 28.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, where does the main strength of traditional project management lie?
A.why: The book says project management is strong on governance and control but gives little focus to product delivery (3.1).

whyNot.0: Product delivery is where agile is strong and project management is light.
whyNot.1: Responding to change is named as a strength of agile, not of project management.
whyNot.3: Self-management of teams is an agile idea; it is not the strength the book gives project management.

A.q: In Version 2, what are business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress called?
A.why: PRINCE2 7 and PRINCE2 Agile V2 call these seven elements practices.

whyNot.0: 'Themes' was the PRINCE2 2017 and Agile V1 term.
whyNot.2: The five focus areas were a V1 heading, and they were not these seven elements.
whyNot.3: The five behaviours were a V1 list (transparency, collaboration and so on), replaced by agile mindset characteristics.

B.q: Which statement about PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
options: It replaces governance with team self-management
It focuses on product delivery and leaves out direction
It is designed mainly for linear-sequential delivery
It covers direction, management and product delivery
B.why: PRINCE2 Agile addresses all three areas (project direction, project management and product delivery) while keeping governance and control throughout (3.1).

whyNot.0: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control; teams self-manage within tolerances.
whyNot.1: Covering only product delivery describes agile frameworks on their own, not PRINCE2 Agile.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile is specifically for iterative and incremental delivery.

B.q: What may a candidate use during the PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner (V2) exam?
options: The Official Book, with their own notes in it
Any printed agile reference book they choose
The Official Book, with no notes written in it
Their own summary notes on separate paper
B.why: Practitioner is open book: the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book only, and candidates may write notes inside it.

whyNot.1: Other books are not allowed; only the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book may be used.
whyNot.2: The V2 syllabus allows notes written inside the book.
whyNot.3: Separate notes are not allowed; notes must be inside the Official Book.

B.q: Which aspect of project performance was added, giving seven aspects in Version 2?
B.why: PRINCE2 7 added sustainability, so V2 has seven aspects: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk.

whyNot.0: Benefits was already one of the six aspects in V1.
whyNot.1: Communication matters greatly in agile, but it is not one of the aspects of project performance.
whyNot.3: Customer value is not one of the seven aspects; the value-related aspect is benefits, which was already in V1.

C.q:
Which two statements about PRINCE2 Agile Version 2 are correct?
1. The Foundation exam is closed book.
2. The Foundation pass mark is 55%.
3. The role set includes a chief product owner and a team coach.
4. The Agilometer belongs to the progress practice.
C.why: Foundation is closed book (1), and the 11 V2 roles include the chief product owner and the team coach (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the V2 Foundation pass mark is 60% (24 of 40); 55% was V1.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: the pass mark is 60%, and the Agilometer sits in the risk practice.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is right, but the Agilometer is a risk practice tool, not a progress one.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A candidate revising from Version 1 material should know that the old 'change' theme is now covered by the [?] practice.
C.why: In Version 2, issues and changes to the baseline are handled by the issues practice.

whyNot.0: The risk practice handles uncertainties, not the control of changes to the baseline.
whyNot.1: The progress practice monitors actual against planned and handles exceptions.
whyNot.2: The plans practice defines what will be delivered and how, when and by whom.

C.q: Which set of figures describes the PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner (V2) exam?
C.why: Practitioner V2 has 50 questions in 150 minutes (188 with extra time) and a pass mark of 30 (60%).

whyNot.1: 28 was the V1 Foundation pass mark, out of 50.
whyNot.2: 40 questions with 24 to pass is the Foundation format, which lasts 60 minutes.
whyNot.3: The Practitioner exam lasts 150 minutes, not 120.

reteach.title: Old guide or new guide?
reteach.question: How can you tell quickly whether a revision source is written for Version 2?

blocks.body: Version 1 sources talk about themes, a six-sided hexagon of aspects, five focus areas, five behaviours and a 50-question Foundation exam. Version 2 sources talk about practices, seven aspects including sustainability, 11 roles such as the chief product owner and team coach, artifacts such as the project canvas and release map, and named workshops for each process.

root.label: A term in your revision guide

blocks.text: Foundation V2 = 40 questions, 24 to pass, 60 minutes. If a source says 50 and 55%, it describes the retired V1 Foundation exam.

explain.body: Forty four-option questions, one mark each, no negative marking. You need 24 (60%). You have 60 minutes, or 75 if you take the exam in a language that is not your own. It is closed book and tests recall and understanding.

test.q: How long is the standard PRINCE2 Agile Foundation (V2) exam, without extra time?
test.why: Foundation lasts 60 minutes; candidates in a non-native language get 25% extra, making 75.

whyNot.0: 75 minutes is the time with the 25% extra-time allowance.
whyNot.1: 90 minutes is not a PRINCE2 Agile exam duration.

explain.body: Project management brings direction, governance and control. Agile brings product delivery and responsiveness to change. PRINCE2 Agile uses both, so all three areas of a project are covered (3.1).

test.q: Agile on its own is strong on product delivery. According to the book, where is it relatively light?
test.why: The book says agile has relatively little focus on project direction and project management (3.1).

whyNot.1: Responding to change is one of agile's strengths.
whyNot.2: Delivering products is agile's main strength.
whyNot.3: Frequent team feedback is central to agile ways of working.

explain.body: The five focus areas, the five behaviours and the six-aspect hexagon are Version 1 headings. Their useful content moved: the Agilometer into the risk practice, contracts into the commercial management approach, rich communication into the mindset and people chapters.

test.q: Which of these is a Version 1 heading that is no longer in the Version 2 syllabus?
test.why: The five focus areas were a V1 heading; V2 spreads their content across practices, people and mindset.

whyNot.0: The project canvas is a new V2 artifact.
whyNot.1: Named workshops for each process are new in V2.
whyNot.2: The seven practices are the V2 name for the old themes.

explain.body: V2 has 11 roles: project executive, chief product owner, senior supplier, project assurance, agile coach, project manager, project support, product owner, team coach, developer and tester. 'Scrum master' is not a PRINCE2 Agile role name; that work fits the team coach.

test.q: Which Version 2 role best fits the work a Scrum master does?
test.why: The team coach works closely with one or two teams and helps them self-manage; a Scrum master fits this role.

whyNot.0: The agile coach works across the organization on systemic blockers, not inside one team.
whyNot.2: The product owner owns the team's product backlog.
whyNot.3: Project support gives administrative help and maintains dashboards.
